svg.title: Multi-cloud secure document platform: Azure identity and API tiers federating into an encrypted AWS document store
svg.desc: A Terraform control plane deploys into an Azure subscription and an AWS account from a single configuration. On the Azure side, Entra ID issues tokens, a user-assigned managed identity holds Key Vault access, and two API Management tiers sit in a virtual network: an external tier that validates JWTs and an internal VNet-injected tier that proxies Key Vault using its own managed identity. On the AWS side, an OIDC provider trusts the Entra issuer and an IAM role accepts AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity when the audience and subject claims match, granting read access scoped to one S3 prefix and decrypt on one customer-managed KMS key. Four negative tests confirm that a wrong identity, an expired token, an out-of-scope prefix and a missing KMS grant are all denied.
svg.text: Azure identity and API tiers federating into an encrypted AWS document store - no stored access keys on either side
One configuration, two providers, one state file
Remote state in an Azure Storage blob, leased on write so two
applies cannot collide. Azure resource groups split by lifecycle
so disposable workloads tear down without touching identity.
RBAC authorisation, not legacy access policies
Key Vault Secrets User · subject of the AWS trust
VNet-injected · managed identity to Key Vault
Trusts the Entra v1.0 issuer for this tenant
Versioned · all four public access blocks on
SSE-KMS default · bucket keys · annual rotation
Unencrypted upload · wrong key · plain HTTP
Deny wins over any IAM allow
Different managed identity assumes the role
Read attempted outside the inbound prefix
AccessDenied - KMS is a separate gate
internal tier reads a secret via its own managed identity
There is no :iss condition key - the issuer is pinned by which provider is named.
Federated role - what it may do
ListBucket is scoped by condition, not by ARN - the bucket ARN has no prefix.
Identity is an added category, in the same muted family as the rest.
The workload asks the local instance metadata endpoint for a token. No credential is sent with the request.
Entra ID returns a signed JWT whose subject claim is the managed identity's principal ID.
The token is presented to AWS STS as AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity against the registered OIDC provider.
The trust policy checks the audience and subject claims, then STS returns short-lived credentials.
Those credentials read objects under the inbound prefix only; listing is scoped by an s3:prefix condition.
S3 asks KMS to unwrap the data key - a second, independent grant.
